reuse.why: The API and existing planning consumers reuse getScheduledAmount, which also reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance helper.

duplication.why: Range selection and approximate-amount planning remain centralized without introducing duplicate calculation blocks.

placement.why: Expected-amount policy stays in shared/schedules.ts, while API serialization and consumer-specific data extraction remain in their existing layers.

scope.why: The changes are focused on schedule amount policy, its API exposure, associated consumers, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The centralized design is straightforward to maintain, although the optional string operator and positional false argument make the helper contract less explicit than a typed interface would.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers delegate expected-amount calculation to getScheduledAmount rather than implementing their own policy.

disguised_duplication.where: The diff shares the calculation directly rather than disguising copies through renamed or reshaped logic.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount replaces rangeRounding with an optional op parameter and adds an isapprox conditional; no changed call site bypasses the helper.
